questions.answer: B) Stratosphere

questions.answer: B) To make and pass state-level laws

questions.answer: B) Farming on a cleared patch of forest and moving to a new patch when soil fertility drops

questions.question_text: Define the term 'Lithosphere' in the context of the Earth's environmental domains. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The lithosphere is the solid, outermost layer of the Earth. It consists of rocks, minerals, and a thin layer of soil, providing land for human settlements and agriculture.

questions.question_text: Who were the 'Mansabdars' in the administrative system of the Mughal Empire? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Mansabdars were individuals holding a 'mansab' or rank within the Mughal administrative framework. They were responsible for maintaining a specified number of cavalrymen and collecting local revenue.

questions.question_text: State one major difference between a public healthcare facility and a private healthcare facility in India. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Public healthcare facilities are run by the government offering free or low-cost treatments, while private facilities are owned by individuals or companies, charging high fees for medical services.

questions.question_text: What is meant by a 'wholesale' market in the chain of economic trading? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A wholesale market is where goods are bought and sold in very large bulk quantities. It acts as a primary link connecting the manufacturer or farmer to the retail traders.

questions.question_text: Explain how the 'putting-out system' functions in the traditional textile weaving industry. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: In the putting-out system, wealthy merchants supply raw yarn to local weavers. The weavers craft the cloth in their homes and return the finished product to the merchants. This saves weavers from buying raw materials but keeps them dependent.

questions.question_text: Describe the geological formation of 'mushroom rocks' typically found in desert environments. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: In deserts, high-speed winds act as active agents of erosion. They erode the lower, softer section of standing rocks much faster than the harder upper part, resulting in a narrow base and a wide top, resembling a mushroom.

questions.question_text: How did the Rashtrakuta dynasty initially rise to political power in the Deccan region? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Initially, the Rashtrakutas were subordinate chieftains to the Chalukyas of Karnataka. In the mid-eighth century, their leader Dantidurga overthrew his Chalukya overlord, performed the 'hiranya-garbha' ritual, and established the independent and powerful Rashtrakuta Empire.

questions.question_text: Why do tropical evergreen forests appear continuously green throughout the entire year? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: These forests are found near the equator where it rains heavily throughout the year. Because there is no distinct dry season, the diverse tree species do not shed their leaves simultaneously, keeping the canopy permanently green.

questions.question_text: Explain the essential role and responsibilities of an MLA (Member of Legislative Assembly) in state governance. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: An MLA is directly elected by the public to represent a specific constituency. They debate issues, raise local concerns in the Legislative Assembly, and vote on new laws, acting as a crucial bridge between citizens and the state government.

questions.question_text: Analyze the major administrative and military strategies used by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj that led directly to the successful rise of the Marathas. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Shivaji Maharaj built highly mobile military units that mastered guerrilla warfare tactics suited for the rugged Western Ghats terrain. He constructed an extensive network of strategic hill forts to secure his borders. Administratively, he set up a structured council of eight ministers known as the Ashta Pradhan and introduced fair revenue collection systems that won widespread regional public loyalty.

questions.question_text: Describe the continuous process of the rock cycle, detailing how one type of rock transforms into another under specific conditions. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The rock cycle is a continuous geological process. Molten magma cools to form igneous rocks. Over time, these break down into sediments that compact into sedimentary rocks. Under extreme heat and pressure, both igneous and sedimentary rocks change into metamorphic rocks, which can eventually melt back into magma, restarting the cycle entirely.

questions.question_text: Discuss the main philosophical teachings of the Bhakti saint Kabir and explain the unique ways in which he expressed his devotion. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Kabir strongly rejected orthodox religious traditions, idol worship, and the rigid caste system of both Hinduism and Islam. He preached belief in a formless Supreme God, emphasizing that salvation is achieved only through true devotion (bhakti). He creatively expressed his profound ideas through short, accessible couplets (dohas) in everyday Hindi, appealing directly to the common masses.

questions.question_text: How does the mass media set the 'agenda' in a democratic society, and why is this power considered highly significant? [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The media sets the 'agenda' by choosing which specific stories or issues deserve front-page attention, thereby shaping public awareness and opinion. This power is highly significant in a democracy because it forces the government to address highlighted public issues, demands accountability, and directly influences how citizens perceive national events and political policies.

questions.question_text: Compare the lifestyle, mobility, and economic activities of nomadic tribes, such as the Banjaras, with those of settled agricultural communities. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Nomadic tribes like the Banjaras were mobile pastoralists and trader-nomads who traveled across regions with their animal caravans. They traded pastoral products like milk and wool for grains and cloth. In contrast, settled agricultural communities lived permanently in villages, tied to their land, relying primarily on seasonal crop cultivation and localized barter systems for their economic survival.

questions.question_text: Explain the harsh climatic conditions of the Sahara Desert and describe how the local inhabitants adapt their daily lives to survive. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The Sahara experiences an extreme scorching climate with incredibly hot days and freezing nights, alongside very scarce rainfall. To survive, nomadic tribes like the Bedouins rear livestock such as camels and goats for milk and hair. They wear heavy robes to protect against violent dust storms and settle temporarily around rare water oases to grow date palms.
